title: Uthman's caliphate
hook: the gentle Uthman rules as lands and a navy grow

segments.voice: Yesterday, Umar's death: struck at the dawn prayer, he left the choice to a council. Your line was a council, not a crown. Did you ask others before deciding something that touched them? Day eight hundred seventy-seven.

Should I not feel shy before a man the angels feel shy before? Sahih Muslim reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, asking that about one of his companions. The scene around it is small. The Prophet is resting at home, his clothes loosely arranged. Abu Bakr comes in, and he stays as he is. Umar comes in, and he stays as he is. Then Uthman asks to enter, and the Prophet sits up and straightens his garment. Aisha asks him why. His answer is that question. The man is Uthman ibn Affan, and after Umar's death the council chose him. Today, the shape of his rule.
screen: `THE PROPHET SITS UP.` → `THE ANGELS FEEL SHY.` → `THE COUNCIL CHOOSES UTHMAN.`

segments.voice: Bukhari records how the choice was made. The men Umar named narrowed it among themselves, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, giving up his own claim, was trusted to choose between Ali and Uthman. He spent nights consulting people, the report says, and in the end he took Uthman's hand and pledged to him, and the people followed. So Uthman began with a reputation already set. In Bukhari's reports he is the one who answered the Prophet's call to provide the well of Rumah for the people, and to equip the army in a time of hardship. Wealthy, quiet, generous, modest. Under his rule the lands of the Muslims kept growing. And something new happened: ships. Bukhari tells of a woman, Umm Haram, who once heard the Prophet describe people of his community riding the sea like kings on thrones. She asked him to pray that she would be one of them. The report says she later sailed, in the days of Mu'awiyah, who served Uthman as governor of Syria, and the histories set that voyage in Uthman's time. Now the harder part. Gentleness in a ruler can be read two ways. His admirers see mercy: a caliph slow to punish, open-handed with his own money. His critics, in his own lifetime, said he gave too many posts to his relatives and was too slow to remove governors people complained about. The sources record both. Sunni Muslims honor him as the third of the rightly guided caliphs and one of the companions promised paradise. Shia Muslims hold that Ali should have led from the start, and Shia tellings dwell on the complaints against Uthman's rule. Both readings are kept here, side by side, with no winner picked, because the complaints will grow, and the next few days will show where they led.
screen: `ABD AL-RAHMAN CONSULTS FOR NIGHTS.` · `A WELL PROVIDED, AN ARMY EQUIPPED.` · `UMM HARAM AND THE SEA.` · `MERCY, OR TOO SOFT?` · then, large: `GENTLE RULE.`

segments.voice: The practice: be gentle in authority. Settle, and breathe. Small kingdoms are everywhere. A kitchen. A classroom. A shift you run. A dog, even. Pick one place where people, or creatures, depend on your decisions. Breathe in, and remember a recent moment there when you were sharper than you needed to be. Breathe out, and picture doing it again, the same decision, but gentler in tone. Same firmness, softer voice. If you pray, you can ask for mercy in how you lead. The bell holds the time.
Uthman's caliphate. The rule of Uthman ibn Affan, chosen by the council after Umar: a modest, generous man, a time of growth and ships at sea, and complaints that would not go away. Today's word.
Your line: gentle rule. Today, give one instruction, to anyone, more gently than you normally would, and see if it still gets done. Day eight hundred seventy-seven.

howItsDone: Sunni Muslims honor Uthman as the third rightly guided caliph and remember his modesty and generosity; Shia Muslims hold that Ali was the rightful leader, and Shia tellings dwell on the complaints against Uthman's rule.

fork.setup: you're the caliph. people complain about a governor who is also your relative. what do you do?
options: keep him and hope the complaints fade.
the sources disagree on what you did.
fork.reveal: the histories record both his defenders and his critics; the complaints about governors grew, and the coming days follow where they led.

original.note: Arabic: the name of the third caliph for Sunni Muslims, Uthman ibn Affan.

trapdoor: what you thought: Uthman was just the caliph between Umar and Ali.
what it means: a modest, generous man chosen by council, whose rule saw lands and sea voyages grow, and complaints grow too.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's account of the council and Umm Haram's sea voyage under Mu'awiyah, and the long Sunni and Shia debate over Uthman's appointments.

notes: Audit: 'the report places the sea voyage in this era' overstated Bukhari (which says only 'in the days of Mu'awiyah'); dating it to Uthman's caliphate is now attributed to the histories (al-Tabari). 'Hold both views without picking a winner' (an instruction to the listener) recast as a description. Note: the earlier note about 'many of their historians are critical' is stale; that wording is no longer in the script.
The hook opens with a paraphrase (no quotation marks) of the Prophet's question in Sahih Muslim 2401; confirm wording.

Hadith numbers cited from memory: confirm Muslim 2401, Bukhari 3700, 2778 (ta'liq on Rumah and the army of hardship), and the Umm Haram reports (2788–2789, 2799–2800). Confirm that the report places her voyage 'in the days of Mu'awiyah'.
The outline's 'rules twelve years' was cut under the claims rule. 'The first ships' was also avoided; the script says only 'ships at sea'.
Sunni and Shia views are given side by side; 'many of their historians are critical' should be confirmed as fair by both Keepers.
The council members are not counted on purpose; yesterday (876) covered the council of six.

Editor: fixed the council account to match Bukhari 3700/7207 (the six narrowed the choice and Abd al-Rahman, withdrawing, chose between Ali and Uthman after nights of consultation, not 'stepped aside one by one' or 'house to house'); the well and army now follow Bukhari 2778's wording (answered the Prophet's call) and the unsourced 'when others could not' is cut; 'a promise kept' narration softened; 'many of their historians' replaced to meet the claims rule; practice list changed so it no longer repeats day 868's; garbled 'That question is his answer' fixed; Tirmidhi 3747 added for 'promised paradise'.
